calls.title: Bryce / Kari
calls.summary: The team discussed various improvements for the feature page's design, emphasizing usability and visual consistency. They agreed to remove the gray background fill from condition groups, gaining an extra 16 pixels of space, and replacing it with a simple border. The modal width will remain at 800 pixels, with a focus on reducing internal padding by at least 20 pixels. Adjustments to the 'And'/'Or' labels were proposed for better consistency, and the 'Add Condition' button size will be reduced to fit the compact layout. The advanced mode's reduced usage prompted a need for clearer status indicators. Teresa's onboarding will focus on key table components, ensuring efficient resource allocation, while timely delivery of mockups will support ongoing design updates.

calls.summary: The team focused on simplifying the feature selector UI and redesigning the feature landing page to improve usability and visual consistency. Bryce Fitzsimons proposed merging feature details into a three-column format, supported by Kari Kay, to enhance readability. Label adjustments, such as simplifying the 'pass if value' label, were also discussed to reduce confusion. The feature landing page will see updates to header styles and reduced clutter, with a focus on consistent font sizes. The migration to Radix components aims to standardize UI elements, while incremental changes will prioritize immediate usability improvements over complex updates. Both Bryce and Kari emphasized the importance of removing features that do not add clear value, aligning with a user-centric design philosophy.

calls.title: Bryce / Kari
calls.summary: The discussion centered on revamping the stale status feature, introducing a four-state system that improves maintenance visibility across all environments, while addressing user concerns about potential confusion from status labels. The integration of usage analytics with staleness calculations was planned, but the team contemplated simplifying environment controls to prevent accidental changes. Additionally, the need for enhanced version control and audit logs was emphasized to meet client expectations, given the importance of tracking changes in larger organizations. Participants agreed on the necessity of reusing design elements to maintain clarity and prevent overload during a period of rapid development, ensuring sustainable design practices while balancing complexity against user experience.

calls.title: Bryce / Kari Check in
calls.summary: The discussion centered on maintaining a clear distinction between rule status and ramp schedule to prevent user confusion. Kari Kay emphasized the importance of a badge only reflecting the rule status, while Bryce Fitzsimons agreed on separating the two concepts in the UI. The team resolved to provide a clear label for the schedule display, termed 'Scheduled Ramp Up', featuring a straightforward end date. They also talked about the system's generation of revisions for auditability in ramping processes, balancing automation with necessary user approvals. The user interface will undergo simplification by eliminating redundant indicators and adopting hover tooltips for detailed information, ultimately supporting better user understanding and integration with continuous integration pipelines.

calls.title: Bryce / Kari
calls.summary: The discussion emphasized the need to restructure the current modal UI for feature rollouts, which is seen as confusing and illogical. Key points included reordering the UI to better align with user workflows, where establishing a rollout approach should precede the percentage and schedule settings. Participants highlighted the importance of consolidating controls to avoid duplication and spread-out inputs, allowing for a smoother user experience. The team agreed on using clearer visual cues to differentiate controlled and uncontrolled states, ensuring visibility of current rollout statuses even when values are locked. Insights revealed that most users prefer quick, direct value settings rather than complex ramping controls, leading to considerations for a more iterative design approach, ensuring future scalability and user-friendly enhancements.
calls.keywords: ramp up, rollout percentage, targeting attributes, UI sequencing, scheduling, presets
calls.action_items:

calls.title: Bryce <> Kari
calls.summary: The team discussed creating a unified review page for feature approvals to consolidate various review actions and comments into one cohesive interface. Key UI elements like revision summaries, author metadata, and status badges were identified to improve clarity. A tabbed layout was proposed to enhance navigation without leaving the feature page. Additionally, a global approval list is being developed to better manage pending reviews. The group also addressed the need for clearer visual representation in namespace targeting, particularly focusing on color clarity for both light and dark modes. Overall, there is an emphasis on simplicity and clarity in design to enhance user understanding and workflow.
